description: Core-Weighted LBD Phase Selection: Step 1: Maintain two independent phase-saving arrays, `phase_focused[v]` and `phase_stable[v]`. During backtracking, update only the array corresponding to the solver's current search mode (focused/exploration vs. stable/exploitation). Step 2: Maintain a phase quality matrix `phase_score[v][2]` (tracking scores for True and False assignments). During conflict analysis, differentiate variable participation: add `2.0 / LBD` to `phase_score[v][assigned_phase]` for variables present in the final learned clause, and add `0.5 / LBD` for variables that are merely resolved away during the conflict resolution. Decay all scores by a factor of 0.95 at every restart. Step 3: Inside `kissat_decide_phase(v)`, identify the current search mode and retrieve the baseline candidate phase: `P = phase_focused[v]` if in focused mode, otherwise `P = phase_stable[v]`. Step 4: Evaluate the historical LBD quality of the candidate phase. If the opposite phase has a significantly better track record—specifically, if `phase_score[v][!P] > 1.5 * phase_score[v][P]` AND `phase_score[v][!P] > 2.0` (minimum confidence threshold)—override the baseline and select `!P`. Step 5: If the override conditions in Step 4 are not met, return the baseline candidate phase `P`.
parent_algorithm_description: Bimodal LBD-Scored Phase Selection: Step 1: Maintain two independent phase-saving arrays, `phase_focused[v]` and `phase_stable[v]`. During backtracking, update only the array corresponding to the solver's current search mode (focused/exploration vs. stable/exploitation). Step 2: Maintain a phase quality matrix `phase_score[v][2]` (tracking scores for True and False assignments). During conflict analysis, for each variable involved in the conflict, add `1.0 / LBD` to `phase_score[v][assigned_phase]`. Decay all scores by a factor of 0.95 at every restart. Step 3: Inside `kissat_decide_phase(v)`, identify the current search mode and retrieve the baseline candidate phase: `P = phase_focused[v]` if in focused mode, otherwise `P = phase_stable[v]`. Step 4: Evaluate the historical LBD quality of the candidate phase. If the opposite phase has a significantly better track record—specifically, if `phase_score[v][!P] > 1.5 * phase_score[v][P]` AND `phase_score[v][!P] > 2.0` (minimum confidence threshold)—override the baseline and select `!P`. Step 5: If the override conditions in Step 4 are not met, return the baseline candidate phase `P`.
analysis: In Step 2 of the original algorithm, all variables involved in the conflict graph receive the exact same LBD-based reward. This variant improves upon Step 2 by differentiating between variables that survive resolution to become part of the final learned clause (the core) and those that are resolved away. Because the final learned clause is what directly prunes the future search space, disproportionately rewarding the phases of its constituent variables yields a much stronger signal for phase quality, leading to more accurate phase overrides in Step 4.
